clue: A crystalline stimulant sweeping across Zimbabwean urban centres. Known for extreme energy, paranoia, and rapid addiction.
definition: Crystal Methamphetamine — a potent synthetic stimulant that floods the brain with dopamine, causing intense euphoria followed by severe crashes, paranoia, and rapid physical deterioration.
legalFramework: Criminal Law Code [Chapter 9:23] Sections 156/157 & Dangerous Drugs Act [Chapter 15:02]. Scheduled synthetic drug.
penalties: Dealing/Supply: 15–20 years imprisonment (mandatory under aggravated circumstances). Possession/Use: Up to 10 years imprisonment.

clue: A mild stimulant leaf commonly chewed in East and Southern Africa. Contains cathinone and cathine.
definition: Khat (Mairungi) — a plant whose leaves contain cathinone, a stimulant similar to amphetamine. Produces mild euphoria, increased alertness, and reduced appetite. Prolonged use leads to psychological dependence.
legalFramework: Dangerous Drugs Act [Chapter 15:02]. Scheduled plant substance due to cathinone/cathine content.
penalties: Dealing: 10–15 years imprisonment under Section 156. Possession: Fines to 10 years imprisonment under Section 157.

clue: A dangerous street-cocktail of heroin mixed with antiretrovirals, rat poison, and other substances. High overdose risk.
definition: Nyaope (Whoonga) — a highly addictive street drug combining low-grade heroin with various cutting agents including ARVs, rat poison, and detergents. Causes severe respiratory depression and has an extremely high overdose fatality rate.
legalFramework: Dangerous Drugs Act [Chapter 15:02] & Criminal Law Code [9:23] Section 156. Prohibited Class A narcotic.
penalties: Dealing/Distribution: 15–20 years imprisonment. Possession/Ingestion: Up to 10 years imprisonment.
statute: Dangerous Drugs Act [15:02] & Criminal Law Code [9:23] §156

clue: A codeine-based cough syrup widely smuggled and abused as a recreational drink. Often mixed with soda.
definition: Broncleer (Bronco) — a prescription cough syrup containing codeine phosphate, an opioid. When consumed in large quantities, it produces sedation, euphoria, and respiratory depression. Highly addictive.
streetNames: Bronco, Lean, Tosein, Codeine, Purple Drank
legalFramework: Medicines and Allied Substances Control Act (MASCA) [Chapter 15:03] & Customs and Excise Act [Chapter 23:02]. Prescription-only Schedule 3/4 medicine.
penalties: Unlawful Importation/Dealing: Fines up to Level 12, confiscation, imprisonment 5–10 years under MASCA §38/100.

clue: An illicit, unlicensed high-proof spirit distilled informally. Known to cause severe health damage including blindness.
definition: Kachasu (Musombodia/Tumbwa) — a dangerous illicit brew with extremely high alcohol content, often containing methanol and other toxic byproducts from improper distillation. Causes liver failure, blindness, and death.
legalFramework: Liquor Act [Chapter 14:12], Traditional Beer Act [14:24], Harmful Liquids Act [14:10]. Distilling or selling unlicensed spirits is strictly illegal.
penalties: Manufacturing/Selling Illicit Spirits: Fines up to Level 7, forfeiture of equipment, imprisonment 1–2 years.

clue: A sedative-hypnotic containing methaqualone, often combined with antihistamines. Known on the street as a powerful downer.
definition: Mandrax (Methaqualone) — a sedative-hypnotic drug that produces relaxation and drowsiness. Frequently combined with diphenhydramine for enhanced sedative effects. Highly addictive with severe withdrawal symptoms.
legalFramework: MASCA [Chapter 15:03] & Dangerous Drugs Act [15:02]. Methaqualone is a prohibited scheduled drug.
penalties: Unlawful possession/sale triggers dangerous drug provisions: Up to 15 years imprisonment.

clue: A class of prescription sedatives used for anxiety and insomnia. Highly addictive when misused.
definition: Benzodiazepines (Diazepam, Valium, Lorazepam) — prescription CNS depressants that enhance GABA activity. Used medically for anxiety and sleep disorders, but widely diverted for recreational use. Dangerous when combined with alcohol.
legalFramework: MASCA [Chapter 15:03]. Controlled prescription substances. Illegal dispensing carries penalties.
penalties: Illegal dispensing of prescription benzos: Up to 5 years imprisonment under MASCA.

clue: The most widely used illicit substance in Zimbabwe. A plant with psychoactive properties, now partially legal for medicinal use.
definition: Cannabis (Mbanje/Dagga/Skunk) — contains THC, which produces euphoria, relaxation, and altered perception. High-potency strains (skunk) carry increased risks of anxiety, paranoia, and psychosis, especially in young users.
streetNames: Dagga, Skunk, Weed, Grass, Ganja, Mbanje
legalFramework: Criminal Law Code [9:23] §§156-158 & SI 62 of 2018. Industrial hemp and medical cannabis legal only under strict Ministry of Health licence.
penalties: Dealing: Fines up to Level 14 or 15 years imprisonment. Cultivation: 10–15 years. Personal Possession: 3–10 years (typically 6–36 months for small amounts).

clue: A condition characterised by persistent, excessive worry that interferes with daily functioning. The most common mental health condition globally.
definition: Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD) — a chronic condition involving excessive, uncontrollable worry about multiple aspects of life, accompanied by restlessness, fatigue, muscle tension, and sleep disturbance. Affects approximately 4% of the population.
legalFramework: Not applicable. Treated through psychotherapy (CBT), medication (SSRIs), and lifestyle modifications.
penalties: N/A — This is a treatable medical condition, not a criminal matter.
statute: Clinical diagnosis per DSM-5 / ICD-11 criteria

clue: A mood disorder causing persistent sadness, loss of interest, and impaired daily function. Leading cause of disability worldwide.
definition: Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) — characterised by at least two weeks of pervasive low mood, anhedonia (loss of pleasure), changes in appetite/sleep, fatigue, feelings of worthlessness, and in severe cases, suicidal ideation.
legalFramework: Not applicable. Managed with antidepressant medication, psychotherapy, and in severe cases, ECT or TMS.
penalties: N/A — This is a treatable medical condition requiring compassionate care.
statute: Clinical diagnosis per DSM-5 / ICD-11 criteria

clue: A serious mental disorder involving hallucinations, delusions, and disorganised thinking. Typically emerges in late adolescence or early adulthood.
definition: Schizophrenia — a chronic brain disorder affecting approximately 1% of the population. Characterised by positive symptoms (hallucinations, delusions), negative symptoms (flat affect, social withdrawal), and cognitive impairments.
legalFramework: Not applicable. Treated with antipsychotic medication, psychosocial support, and community-based care.
penalties: N/A — This is a severe medical condition. Stigma and lack of access to care remain major barriers in SADC.
statute: Clinical diagnosis per DSM-5 / ICD-11 criteria

clue: A persistent, chronic form of depression lasting two years or more. Less severe than major depression but longer-lasting.
definition: Persistent Depressive Disorder (Dysthymia) — a continuous, long-term form of depression where the individual experiences a depressed mood most of the day, for more days than not, over at least two years. Often goes undiagnosed.
legalFramework: Not applicable. Treatment includes long-term psychotherapy and antidepressant medication.
penalties: N/A — Early detection and consistent treatment significantly improve outcomes.
statute: Clinical diagnosis per DSM-5 / ICD-11 criteria

clue: An anxiety disorder where individuals fear and avoid places or situations that might cause panic, helplessness, or embarrassment.
definition: Agoraphobia — intense fear of being in situations where escape might be difficult or help unavailable. Commonly involves fear of open spaces, public transport, crowds, or being outside alone. Often develops after panic attacks.
legalFramework: Not applicable. Treatment involves graduated exposure therapy, CBT, and sometimes SSRIs.
penalties: N/A — With proper treatment, most individuals can significantly reduce avoidance behaviours.
statute: Clinical diagnosis per DSM-5 / ICD-11 criteria

clue: The key Zimbabwean statute controlling medicines, allied substances, and pharmaceutical regulation.
definition: Medicines and Allied Substances Control Act [Chapter 15:03] — the primary legislation governing the regulation of medicines, medical devices, and allied substances in Zimbabwe. Establishes the Medicines Control Authority of Zimbabwe (MCAZ).
legalFramework: MASCA [Chapter 15:03] empowers MCAZ to register, regulate, and control the importation, manufacture, distribution, and sale of medicines.
penalties: Violations under MASCA can result in fines, seizure of products, licence revocation, and imprisonment up to 10 years depending on the offence.
statute: Medicines and Allied Substances Control Act [Chapter 15:03]

clue: A legal classification term for drugs that induce stupor, insensibility, or sleep. Heavily regulated under Zimbabwean and international law.
definition: Narcotic — a term derived from the Greek "narkotikos" (to make numb). Legally refers to opium, opiates, and their derivatives. Under the Dangerous Drugs Act, narcotics are strictly controlled substances with severe penalties for unauthorised possession or dealing.
legalFramework: Dangerous Drugs Act [Chapter 15:02] classifies narcotics as Part I/II scheduled substances. International conventions (Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs 1961) also apply.
penalties: Dealing in narcotics: 15–20 years imprisonment. Possession: Up to 10 years imprisonment under Criminal Law Code §157.
statute: Dangerous Drugs Act [15:02] & Criminal Law Code [9:23]

clue: A substance that reduces excitement, induces calmness, and promotes sleep. Many are prescription-controlled.
definition: Sedative — a drug that depresses the central nervous system, producing calming effects. Includes benzodiazepines, barbiturates, and certain antihistamines. Medically used for anxiety, insomnia, and seizure control. High abuse potential when used without supervision.
legalFramework: MASCA [Chapter 15:03] regulates all sedatives as prescription-only medicines. Unauthorised dispensing or possession is illegal.
penalties: Illegal distribution: Fines and imprisonment up to 5 years under MASCA. Combining sedatives with other drugs can lead to fatal respiratory depression.
